chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a virgin woman, whom they claimed had committed adultery. He ordered the women to look at her, and they said, 'She is a virgin.' He said, 'I would not strike the one upon whom is the seal of God.' And he accepted the testimony of women in such cases.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali determine if a woman accused of adultery was a virgin, and what was the legal consequence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) pragmatic application of *zann* (presumption) and the acceptance of women's testimony (*shahadat al-nisa*) in specific contexts, diverging from the strict requirement of four male witnesses for *hadd* punishment. By citing the 'seal of God' (*khatam min Allah*), the Imam emphasizes divine confirmation of her status, illustrating a nuanced juristic approach where physical verification by women suffices to negate the penalty. This incident is frequently cited by Shia jurists to support the validity of women's testimony in matters of personal status and lineage.
